chapter: Central High, first records and leaving home
title: The boys go north; her 1934 visit to Buffalo and first singing at the Spiderweb
summary: The school band members left Louisville for Cleveland and Buffalo. Just out of high school, she visited Luke Stewart and his wife in Buffalo and was pushed to sing at the Spiderweb with Al Sears's band, her first New York State appearance with a microphone.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: That's when the different boys found, set out for different bands I guess?
Yeah, they did.
Different bands probably came and heard them and hired them.
Yeah. And then alot of them just left Louieville and came on to New York.
Really?
And I know first they went to Cleveland.
Who did?
All of them.
Oh, they did.
Yeah. And then they came to Buffalo and I was out of school then and I came to Buffalo to visit, who was that? The best guitar player I . . .
Luke Stewart.
Luke Stewart and his wife, Martha.

He was a good guitar player?
Oh, he was one of the greatest.
Was he?
And I'm just so sorry he didn't keep on because he was wonderful.
Was he.
Yes. So while I was out visiting we went to a club called The Spiderweb. They took me out that night, you know.
You were just out of High School?

Yeah. Well I had gotten a little job in Louisville and I was going to take a vacation. I saved up my money and I was going up to visit with them. And they took me to this place called the Spiderweb that night and they said, you got to get up and sing. I said, I can't get up and sing here in New York.
It wasn't New York, it was Buffalo.
It was Buffalo, New York.
Oh, I see.
So I said, I don't want to get up there and sing. And they said, oh come on, we want them to hear you. I said, well I'm scared. And they went on

What did you sing, do you remember?
I don't know. I sang a lot of songs. I sang little ballads, you know. I don't remember any of the songs that I sang.
And you told Al sears what key you were going to sing in and so on?
Yeah, and they just played and I just sang, and we had a good time.
Was there a microphone there, do you remember?
Yeah, they had a microphone. In New York, at least, they had mikes.
Yeah, I'm just trying to think when that might have been.
That was in '36, 1936, no '34.
Yeah, because you were still in your early twenties. You must have only been about 21 or 22, don't you think?
Yeah.
See, in '32 you would have been about
